name: Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type 5

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type 5

criteria.description: Calcification of the interosseous membranes of the forearm and lower leg
Radiographic appearance of mesh-like or 'cloudy' bone in long bones
Exuberant hyperplastic callus formation following fractures
Absence of blue sclerae, differentiating from other OI types
Normal type I collagen biochemical studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of interosseous membrane calcification, mesh-like cortical bone on imaging, and hyperplastic callus formation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for IFITM5 mutation can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Exuberant and excessive callus formation unique to OI type 5
Radiographically visible calcification between radius and ulna or tibia and fibula

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mesh-like or 'cloudy' appearance of cortical bone on radiographs
pathognomonic.notes: Distinctive radiographic pattern differentiating from other OI types

common.symptomName: Multiple bone fractures with minimal trauma
searchTerms: many broken bones from minor injuries

common.notes: Increased range of motion in multiple joints

common.symptomName: Bone deformities (e.g., bowing of long bones)

common.notes: Absence of blue sclerae typical of other OI types

occasional.notes: Conductive or mixed hearing loss may develop in adolescence or adulthood

occasional.symptomName: Dental abnormalities (dentinogenesis imperfecta absent or mild)
occasional.notes: Less frequent than in other OI types
searchTerms: tooth problems without severe dentin defects
normal or slight tooth structure changes

rare.symptomName: Respiratory complications due to chest deformities
rare.notes: Restrictive lung disease secondary to skeletal deformities
searchTerms: breathing problems due to chest shape
difficulty breathing related to chest structure

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to vertebral fractures

laboratory: Normal type I collagen biochemical analysis
Normal serum calcium and phosphate levels
imaging: Calcification of interosseous membranes on X-ray
Mesh-like or cloudy appearance of cortical bone
Hyperplastic callus formation at fracture sites
Bowing and deformities of long bones
other: Absence of blue sclerae differentiates from other OI types
Exuberant callus formation may mimic osteosarcoma radiographically

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of interosseous membrane calcification and hyperplastic callus
Normal sclerae but no interosseous membrane calcification
Heterotopic ossification of skin and deep connective tissues

redFlags: Calcification of interosseous membranes causing restricted forearm movement
references: Forlino A, Marini JC. Osteogenesis imperfecta. Lancet. 2016;387(10028):1657-1671.
Cho TJ, Lee KE, Lee SK, et al. Osteogenesis imperfecta type V: clinical and genetic features. J Bone Miner Res. 2008;23(7):1100-1106.
